vignette: A 66-year-old man describes electric shocks in his right cheek and jaw lasting a second, set off by chewing and by touching a spot beside his nose. Between attacks he has no pain and the examination, including the corneal reflex, is normal.
stem: Which nerve divisions are involved and what is the usual cause?

options.text: V2 and V3; vascular compression of the trigeminal root

explanation: Paroxysmal lancinating pain with trigger zones in the maxillary and mandibular territories and a normal examination is classic trigeminal neuralgia, usually from compression of the root entry zone by a loop of the superior cerebellar artery.
